newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ long bonds reel in spreads at close, bills flat.
newsitem.headline: NZ long bonds reel in spreads at close, bills flat.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.78 (PREV 92.82) 90-DAYS 7.03 (PREV 7.03)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.55 PCT (PREV 6.55) US 5-YR 6.80 (PREV 6.83)
* NZ long bonds narrow spreads to dollar bloc at close
* Short end held back by downward correction in TWI
* Some dealers see 11/06 breaking back up through 8 pct
New Zealand long bonds rallied sharply at Tuesday's close to finish an impressive 16 basis points lower in yield at 7.93 percent.
The bonds trimmed 13 points off the yield spread against U.S. 10-year Treasuries, to 106 basis points over.

"The bonds were aggressively bought at the long end. It looked like someone was trying to get a curve steepening trade off, so they'd previously sold the long bonds and bought short bonds, and now...they bought the long bonds down hard for a start and tried to get out of the short bonds," one dealer said.
"I don't know how successful they were -- just on the close it looked like someone was putting a reverse trade on."
In the mid part of the curve the 02/00s rallied four basis points to 7.60 percent while the 02/01s rallied six to 7.67 percent.

Lead manager CS First Boston said this morning the rate set for a TeleNote issue by a unit of Telecom Corporation of New Zealand had been struck at 8.73 percent, against the government 04/04s yielding 8.01 percent at the time.
The 04/04 bond rallied five basis points in the afternoon, to end at 7.96 percent.
The money market lagged behind, losing energy after its recent strong performance.
The key 90-day bank bills ended flat at 7.03 percent, after an initial burst of enthusiasm at the open took them below 7.00 percent.
Dealers said the short end had been hampered on the day by a drop in the currency's Trade-Weighted Index below 69. It ended at 68.97, against its 69.09 open and 69.18 close on Monday.
The front futures contract ended four basis points weaker at 92.78 on substantial volume of 2,563 contracts traded.
One dealer said the short end would probably hover around current levels for a while, held in check by the currency.

"And I'm not convinced the long end is all joy and roses down there now -- I think it's going to go back over eight percent...so we'll see the yield curve steepen up again." ---------------------------(SPREADS)----------------------------
